track.goldengate.fact: The bridge opened in 1937. Its opening celebrations gave pedestrians a day on the span before motor traffic began.
track.bayshore-101.fact: Beside this stretch of Highway 101, the Palo Alto Baylands Nature Preserve protects one of the largest undisturbed marshlands left in San Francisco Bay.
track.twin-peaks.fact: Twin Peaks is San Francisco’s second-highest hill area after Mount Davidson. Its grasslands preserve a glimpse of the hills before urban development.
track.lombard.fact: Lombard’s famous block squeezes eight hairpin turns between Hyde and Leavenworth Streets. The rest of the street is much straighter.
track.fishermans-wharf.fact: Behind the visitor attractions is a working fishing heritage. Generations of local fishing families shaped this part of the waterfront.
track.shoreline.fact: Nearby Shoreline park opened in 1983, with much of its land over a closed landfill. Recreation and wildlife habitat replaced the old dumping ground.
track.wolfe-pruneridge.fact: The real circular building and its surrounding parkland were designed together. This game turns the roof into a driving loop; that part is our invention.
track.moffett-field.fact: Moffett Federal Airfield has two parallel runways. Hangar One opened in 1933 for the USS Macon airship and stands 194 feet high.

track.bayshore-101.name: 101 Rush Hour
track.bayshore-101.blurb: Head north on Highway 101 beside Moffett Field's giant hangar, pass the Mountain View, Palo Alto and Menlo Park campuses, and exit at Marsh Road.
track.twin-peaks.name: Twin Peaks
track.twin-peaks.blurb: Up the hill until the whole city is under you.
track.lombard.name: Lombard Street
track.lombard.blurb: Eight hairpins in one block, then down to the bay.
track.fishermans-wharf.name: Fisherman's Wharf
track.fishermans-wharf.blurb: Look back to the Golden Gate, pass Alcatraz, then chase the Bay Bridge down the waterfront.
track.shoreline.name: Big Tech Campus
track.shoreline.blurb: Circle the amphitheatre parkway, tent-roof offices and leafy courtyards.
track.wolfe-pruneridge.name: Big Tech Rooftop
track.wolfe-pruneridge.blurb: Three laps around a 460-metre roof ring, with the whole courtyard inside.
track.moffett-field.name: Research Center
track.moffett-field.blurb: Charge up the main runway, take Taxiway C around Hangar One, and loop past the seven-type aircraft fleet.

car.micro-hatch.name: Sedan
car.micro-hatch.desc: A rounded roof and sweeping rear profile. Ordinary family-car pace, predictable brakes and stable traction.
car.micro-hatch.drive: stable early throttle at ordinary family-car pace
car.sports-car.name: High-performance sports
car.sports-car.desc: Low, wide and built for the fastest straights. Watch out for springy purple splitting slimes.
car.sports-car.drive: power rotates the tail; careful throttle pays
car.lightweight-sports.name: Lightweight sports
car.lightweight-sports.desc: Short, light and precise. Trades some straight-line speed for quick cornering rhythm.
car.lightweight-sports.drive: a light rear end that changes direction quickly
car.jeep.name: Off-roader
car.jeep.desc: Short wheelbase, tall cabin. Pushes through sticky ground.
car.jeep.drive: four driven tyres, with a tall body's movement
car.pickup-travel-trailer.name: Pickup + trailer
car.pickup-travel-trailer.desc: A long bed and a full travel trailer. Leave room for the rear axle.
car.pickup-travel-trailer.drive: steady towing traction; the trailer remains passive
car.monster-truck.name: Monster Truck
car.monster-truck.desc: A lifted pickup on giant tyres, with long-travel suspension and a deep V8 rumble.
car.monster-truck.drive: giant tyres pull together under a slow, tall chassis
car.school-bus.name: School bus
car.school-bus.desc: Heavy and long. Brake early and give corners some room.
car.school-bus.drive: rear driven, mild power and no drift-car snap
car.retro-van.name: Retro van
car.retro-van.desc: Seafoam and warm white. Its tall body rewards smooth steering.
car.retro-van.drive: gentle rear drive rewards smooth throttle
car.city-pod.drive: easy to place; too much power pushes the nose wide

shortcut.safari: Open the game’s itch.io page in Safari. Open the page menu, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen and Add.

shortcut.embedded: Open the game’s itch.io page in Safari on iPhone or Chrome on Android. If this app cannot open it, copy the game link and paste it into your browser. Then use the browser’s Add to Home Screen menu.
shortcut.desktop: Bookmark the game’s itch.io page in your browser to come back later. On a phone, open that page in Safari or Chrome to add a home-screen shortcut.
